frames.narration: You declare the desired state: deployment web, 6 replicas, each pod requesting 1000m CPU. Every node has 4000m. Nothing is running yet.
The controller compares desired (6) with actual (0) and asks the API server to create 6 pod objects. They exist but have no node yet, so they are Pending.
The scheduler filters out nodes without 1000m free, then scores the rest. With a spread policy each pod goes to the emptiest node, so the pods land 2, 2, 1, 1.
Each node's kubelet starts its containers. Once a readiness probe passes, a pod receives traffic. Actual state now equals desired: 6 of 6 ready.
Node 2 loses power. Its 2 pods are gone with it. After about 40 s of missed heartbeats the control plane marks the node NotReady and stops counting its pods.
The controller's loop sees 4 actual against 6 desired. It does not care why. It creates 2 new pods.
Node 1 has 2000m free, Nodes 3 and 4 have 3000m. Spread scoring picks Nodes 3 and 4, and the pods land there. Node 2 is filtered out because it is not Ready.
The new pods pass their readiness probes and join the Service. Back to 6 of 6 with no human involved. Three nodes now hold 12 pods at most; asking for 14 replicas would leave 2 Pending.
